ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, with the hypotenuse $AB$ of the right-angled $\triangle ABC$ as one side, construct a square $ABED$ on the right side of $AB$, with the diagonals of the square intersecting at point $O$. Connect $CO$. If $AC=4$ and $CO=6$, what is the length of $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As illustrated, extend $CB$ to the point $G$, such that $BG=AC=4$,\\
$\because$ according to the problem, quadrilateral $ABED$ is a square,\\
$\therefore \angle 4=\angle 5=45^\circ$, $\angle$EBA$=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle 1+\angle 2=90^\circ$,\\
Furthermore, $\because \triangle ABC$ is a right-angled triangle with $AB$ being the hypotenuse,\\
$\therefore \angle 2+\angle 3=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle 1=\angle 3$,\\
$\because \angle 1+\angle 5=\angle 3+\angle 4$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAO=\angle GBO$,\\
In $\triangle CAO$ and $\triangle GBO$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}CA=GB \\ \angle CAO=\angle GBO \\ AO=BO \end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle CAO \cong \triangle GBO$ (SAS),\\
$\therefore CO=GO=6$, $\angle 6=\angle 8$,\\
$\because \angle 7+\angle 8=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle 6+\angle 7=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle COG=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore CG=\sqrt{6^2+6^2}=6\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore BC=CG-BG=6\sqrt{2}-4$.\\
Thus, the answer is: $BC=\boxed{6\sqrt{2}-4}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, A and B are the two left vertices of the square ABED, E is at the upper right, D is at the lower right, and the two diagonals AE and BD intersect at O; point C is on the left side of the square, C is connected with A and B to form triangle ABC, and segment CO is drawn in the figure. The auxiliary point G is not in the original figure, and needs to be constructed on ray CB according to the method, on the outside of B. Reasoning: Extend CB to G, so that BG=AC=4. Because ABED is a square, O is the intersection point of the diagonals, so AO=BO, and the diagonal of a square forms 45° with a side, and AB⊥BE. Also because △ABC is a right triangle with AB as the hypotenuse, ∠ACB=90°, so the two acute angles of △ABC are complementary. Combining that G, B, C are collinear and AB⊥BE, by angle chasing one obtains ∠CAO=∠GBO. Therefore, in △CAO and △GBO, CA=GB, AO=BO, and the included angle ∠CAO=∠GBO, so △CAO≅△GBO (SAS). Therefore GO=CO=6, and by the corresponding angle relationship combined with the fact that the two diagonals of the square are perpendicular to each other, one can obtain ∠COG=90°. Therefore △COG is an isosceles right triangle whose two legs are both 6, CG=√(6^2+6^2)=6√2. Because C, B, G are collinear and BG=4, BC=CG−BG=6√2−4.
